sections.title: A two-appointments lifecycle demonstration
paragraphs:
Use this original test card in an authorized demonstration. All identifiers below are fictional. It is designed to reveal whether the service can manage the intended existing record, rather than merely create another appointment. No provider has been tested with it here.

**Starting state:** Test customer `CUSTOMER-DEMO-01` has appointment `APPT-A` at the North location and appointment `APPT-B` at the South location. Give each a different date and purpose. The caller asks to move only `APPT-B` and then cancel the moved appointment.

| Stage | Required action | Evidence to capture | Pass boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Locate | Identify the customer using the approved verification method; find both appointments | Customer reference; `APPT-A`; `APPT-B`; location/date for each | No record changed during lookup |
| 2. Select | Have the caller identify the intended appointment | Selected old ID: ___; caller-approved appointment details: ___ | Selection is `APPT-B`, not simply the first matching name |
| 3. Move | Reschedule only the selected appointment | Old ID: ___; resulting ID: ___; old/new times: ___; actor: ___ | `APPT-A` unchanged; one authoritative moved appointment; old slot handled according to the platform’s model |
| 4. Inspect | Read the resulting record from the scheduling system | Status, location, time and record reference: ___ | Evidence matches the requested move before confirming success |
| 5. Fail cancellation | In a supported test environment, simulate a rejected cancellation | Requested ID: ___; error/result: ___; actual appointment status: ___ | No “cancelled” statement; request marked pending with an assigned owner |
| 6. Resolve | Authorized operator completes or declines the pending action | Cancellation confirmation/reference: ___; final state: ___; customer notified: ___ | Success stated only after final status is established |

Some systems retain an appointment's ID when it moves; others create a replacement record. Either can be acceptable if the old-to-new relationship is recorded and the final schedule contains exactly the intended active appointment. Do not require a new ID solely to make the test card look complete.

If the vendor cannot simulate a failure safely, ask it to demonstrate the documented exception process without altering real appointments. Mark the failure behavior untested. A sales promise should not become a passed test.

Suggested wording for the failed-cancellation step: “Your cancellation request is pending. The appointment has not yet been confirmed as cancelled. Our scheduling team will review it.” Your business should set any follow-up commitment; the receptionist should not invent one.

If cancellation is essential, make cancellation evidence a purchase condition rather than a post-launch discovery.

Use the [appointment booking guide](/ai-answering-service/appointment-booking) to define your office’s booking rules. A request might reach the wrong branch, a write might succeed after the connection times out, or an employee might change the appointment while the agent is preparing an update.

sections.title: 1. Put the authoritative record inside the boundary
paragraphs:
Name the destination that owns the appointment or job. If a field-service system owns dispatch capacity and a separate calendar mirrors it, a calendar event alone cannot satisfy your acceptance rule. Document which system wins when they disagree.

Carry these identifiers through intake, writes, retries and exceptions:

- An immutable request ID for the caller’s requested operation.
- The authoritative customer and service-location IDs, rather than name-only matching.
- The branch and destination calendar IDs selected from an approved mapping.
- The appointment or job ID returned by, or validly assigned for, the destination.
- The requested local time, IANA time zone and explicit UTC offset.
- The version read before changing an existing record.

The request ID ties attempts together. It does not prove the caller’s identity, reserve a time slot or make a second customer’s competing request disappear. Store only the information necessary for the operation and keep credentials out of transcripts and diagnostic bundles.

sections.title: 2. Use a state model with an uncertainty branch
paragraphs:
The following is a proposed application model. Names are internal states, not Google Calendar API statuses.

```text
REQUESTED
    | validate identity, branch, operation and permissions
    v
ELIGIBILITY_CHECKED
    | inspect every required availability result
    v
AVAILABILITY_OBSERVED
    | record operation ID and intended payload before sending
    v
WRITE_PENDING ------------------- timeout ----------------> WRITE_UNCERTAIN
    | successful write response                                |
    v                                                          | reconcile by stable ID
PERSISTED_RECORD_INSPECTED <------------------------------------+
    | exact destination, customer/location, time and operation verified
    | no newer cancellation or superseding request
    v
CONFIRMED

Validation failure, incomplete availability, stale version,
unresolved write, or mismatched persisted record -> EXCEPTION_OWNED

Cancellation requested while WRITE_PENDING or WRITE_UNCERTAIN:
record cancellation intent -> suppress booking confirmation -> reconcile write
-> authorized cancellation -> verify destination state -> CANCELLED
                                      |
                                      +-> failure -> EXCEPTION_OWNED
```

Do not silently move from `WRITE_UNCERTAIN` back to a fresh insertion. Inspect the original destination and operation identity first. If reconciliation remains inconclusive, leave a named exception owner and tell the caller the office must verify the request.

In Google Calendar, a free/busy query returns availability information for specified calendars. Its response can contain errors for individual calendars. Inspect those entries even when the overall request returns successfully. A missing or errored calendar must not become an empty busy list in your application. The query supplies information, not a reservation. [Google Calendar free/busy reference](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/v3/reference/freebusy/query)

sections.title: 3. Define the contract before choosing credentials
paragraphs:
Use this proposed contract as a reviewable CSV. The owner column identifies who resolves a mismatch, not who receives every notification. Replace the synthetic values with authorized test identifiers before exercising a real connection.

```csv
field,source_of_truth,example,validation,expected_write,exception_owner
request_id,intake operation ledger,req-001,immutable across retries,operation ledger only,integration lead
customer_id,customer system,cust-001,unique authorized match,reference on destination,office scheduler
location_id,service-location system,loc-001,belongs to customer,reference on destination,office scheduler
branch_id,approved routing map,branch-east,maps to permitted calendar,branch reference,branch administrator
calendar_id,destination configuration,cal-east,exact authorized branch mapping,target resource,integration lead
time_zone,branch configuration,America/New_York,local time and offset agree,event time zone,office scheduler
start,caller-approved request,2026-11-02T09:00:00-05:00,round-trip local time is identical,event start,office scheduler
end,approved duration rule,2026-11-02T10:00:00-05:00,after start and approved duration,event end,office scheduler
record_id,destination or supported ID allocator,event-001,stable reconciliation reference,one intended record,integration lead
expected_version,last authoritative read,v1,matches current version before edit,conditional change,integration lead
permissions,authorized access configuration,event read and write,operation allowed on target calendar,no permission escalation,account administrator
operation,caller-approved operation,create,create or change or cancel,only intended mutation,office scheduler
exception_owner,approved operations roster,office-scheduler-east,assigned before testing,exception queue record,operations manager
```

The sample `record_id` is an illustrative application value, not a claim that its format is valid for every API. Follow the destination’s identifier rules. Preserve the external record ID and operation ID separately when they differ.

### Separate availability access from mutation access

| Test requirement | Google Calendar example | Contract question |
|---|---|---|
| Inspect availability | `calendar.events.freebusy` covers availability on accessible calendars | Which exact calendars may this identity inspect? |
| Read event details | `calendar.events.readonly` | Can the integration locate and verify the intended record? |
| Create, change and delete events | `calendar.events.owned` applies to owned calendars; other configurations require their appropriate scope | Does the authorized identity have the required operation on this destination? |
| Change sharing or calendar configuration | Separate ACL/calendar scopes exist | Why would a booking connection need this administrative power? |

Google recommends the narrowest scopes that meet the application’s requirements. Its permission model is an example, not a portable permission specification for every scheduling product. Do not request account-wide administration merely to resolve a failed booking test. [Google Calendar authorization scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/auth)

sections.title: 4. Test three different concurrency problems
paragraphs:
**One request delivered twice.** Keep the same operation identity and reconcile an existing result. If the destination supports client-assigned identifiers, follow its collision rules. A duplicate-identifier response requires inspection of the existing record, not an automatic new identifier that creates another appointment.

**Two customers choosing the same opening.** Their request IDs are different. Both might observe free time before either writes. Your authoritative scheduling system needs its own supported capacity-control mechanism. A stable request ID alone offers no protection against this race; a bare read/write calendar pair does not guarantee exclusive booking.

**An employee editing an existing appointment.** Read its version, submit a conditional modification and resolve changes rather than overwriting them blindly. Google Calendar supports `If-Match` with the previously read `etag` for update/delete operations. A changed resource produces HTTP 412. Conditional insertion is different: the documented insert safeguard concerns an existing resource ID, not two events occupying the same time. [Google Calendar resource versioning](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/version-resources)

sections.title: 5. Give each failure a bounded recovery path
paragraphs:
| Failure | Proposed application behavior |
|---|---|
| Invalid payload | Correct the input; do not loop on the same invalid request. |
| Missing authorization or access | Stop that operation and route to the authorized administrator; never broaden credentials automatically. |
| Duplicate identifier | Inspect the existing record and compare the intended operation before deciding whether it is the same result. |
| Stale record version | Read the current record and resolve the competing change; do not blindly overwrite it. |
| Rate limiting | Use the platform’s documented backoff guidance with an explicit attempt/time budget and exception owner. |
| Write timeout | Treat persistence as unknown; reconcile before any retry that could create another record. |
| Cancellation failure | Keep cancellation pending until the authoritative destination supplies sufficient evidence of the intended state. |

Google documents invalid-request errors, duplicate IDs, stale-version failures, and rate-limit responses including 403/429. Error reasons matter alongside HTTP status; a 403 is not always the same problem. Its guidance includes exponential backoff for retryable failures. Set a bounded application policy rather than promising indefinite recovery. The uncertainty handling above is a proposed design, not a claim that a timeout proves success or failure. [Google Calendar error handling](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/errors)

sections.title: 6. Run the synthetic failure fixtures
paragraphs:
Use invented customers and a provider-supported test environment. The companion local fixture runner models the acceptance rules without network access or credentials. It tests a deliberately small reference model, not a live connector, API compliance, or production concurrency. The model uses one synthetic east branch and rejects stale updates; successful appointment changes are intentionally unsupported rather than simulated as verified writes. An integration team must replay equivalent failures against its authorized adapter before signing off.

| Fixture and injected condition | Expected authoritative result | Caller wording | Owner and required evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duplicate request: deliver `req-001` twice | One intended record; both deliveries resolve to its ID | “Your appointment is confirmed” only after verification | Integration lead: request-to-record mapping and record count |
| Wrong branch: route east request to west calendar | No new record | “The office needs to verify the location before confirming” | Branch administrator: approved map and rejected target |
| Partial availability: one required calendar returns an error | No new record | “I cannot verify that opening yet” | Integration lead: per-calendar response and exception ID |
| Calendar unavailable: destination lookup cannot complete | No new record or assumed availability | “The office must verify availability” | Integration lead: lookup failure and retry/exception decision |
| Local-time mismatch: New York November time supplied with the wrong offset | No new record | “Let’s verify the local time before confirming” | Scheduler: local time, zone, offset and conversion |
| Stale update: employee edits version 1 into version 2 before agent writes | Employee’s version preserved; change remains unresolved | “Your requested change is pending review” | Scheduler: both versions and rejected conditional update |
| Write timeout after persistence | Original record recovered; no second record | Confirmation only after inspection of that record | Integration lead: original operation ID, timeout and read-back |
| Write timeout before persistence, reconciliation unavailable | No confirmation and no speculative replacement write | “Your request is awaiting verification” | Integration lead: uncertainty state and assigned exception |
| Cancellation during pending creation, then failed cancellation | Persisted record remains active; cancellation stays pending; booking confirmation suppressed | “Your cancellation request is pending verification” | Scheduler: cancellation intent, resulting record and failure |

For a successful cancellation, replace the injected failure with a verified terminal result and assert that no active booking remains. A not-found response by itself may reflect access or lookup problems; use the destination’s documented behavior and your identity checks before treating it as cancellation evidence.

Run the supplied offline file with `python centralized-scheduling-fixtures.py` using a Python installation with IANA time-zone data. Passing assertions establish only that this small reference model meets its fixtures; they do not certify your selected connector.

sections.title: 7. Accept the connection only with evidence
paragraphs:
Require an operation log that connects the input, authorized destination, attempted mutation, inspected result, customer message and exception owner. Mask personal data in review copies. Reject a test that passes only because the system sends reassuring language while the destination is unknown.

Stop testing and disable the affected mutation path if it writes to an unintended branch, loses a competing edit or duplicates a request. Preserve evidence and reconcile affected records through an authorized operator; do not run a bulk-delete “rollback” against live calendars.

**Next step:** establish what your office means by a requested versus confirmed appointment in the [appointment-booking guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/appointment-booking), then give this record contract to the team implementing your chosen connection. For platform-specific evaluation, use the [Jobber answering-service guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/jobber-answering-service) or [ServiceTitan answering-service guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/servicetitan-answering-service). These links are buying-context resources, not proof that any particular integration passes these tests.

- The appointment or job ID returned by, or validly assigned for, the destination.
- The requested local time, IANA time zone and explicit UTC offset.
- The version read before changing an existing record.

The request ID ties attempts together. It does not prove the caller’s identity, reserve a time slot or make a second customer’s competing request disappear. Store only the information necessary for the operation and keep credentials out of transcripts and diagnostic bundles.

## 2. Use a state model with an uncertainty branch

The following is a proposed application model. Names are internal states, not Google Calendar API statuses.

```text
REQUESTED
    | validate identity, branch, operation and permissions
    v
ELIGIBILITY_CHECKED
    | inspect every required availability result
    v
AVAILABILITY_OBSERVED
    | record operation ID and intended payload before sending
    v
WRITE_PENDING ------------------- timeout ----------------> WRITE_UNCERTAIN
    | successful write response                                |
    v                                                          | reconcile by stable ID
PERSISTED_RECORD_INSPECTED <------------------------------------+
    | exact destination, customer/location, time and operation verified
    | no newer cancellation or superseding request
    v
CONFIRMED

Validation failure, incomplete availability, stale version,
unresolved write, or mismatched persisted record -> EXCEPTION_OWNED

Cancellation requested while WRITE_PENDING or WRITE_UNCERTAIN:
record cancellation intent -> suppress booking confirmation -> reconcile write
-> authorized cancellation -> verify destination state -> CANCELLED
                                      |
                                      +-> failure -> EXCEPTION_OWNED
```

Do not silently move from `WRITE_UNCERTAIN` back to a fresh insertion. Inspect the original destination and operation identity first. If reconciliation remains inconclusive, leave a named exception owner and tell the caller the office must verify the request.

In Google Calendar, a free/busy query returns availability information for specified calendars. Its response can contain errors for individual calendars. Inspect those entries even when the overall request returns successfully. A missing or errored calendar must not become an empty busy list in your application. The query supplies information, not a reservation. [Google Calendar free/busy reference](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/v3/reference/freebusy/query)

## 3. Define the contract before choosing credentials

Use this proposed contract as a reviewable CSV. The owner column identifies who resolves a mismatch, not who receives every notification. Replace the synthetic values with authorized test identifiers before exercising a real connection.

```csv
field,source_of_truth,example,validation,expected_write,exception_owner
request_id,intake operation ledger,req-001,immutable across retries,operation ledger only,integration lead
customer_id,customer system,cust-001,unique authorized match,reference on destination,office scheduler
location_id,service-location system,loc-001,belongs to customer,reference on destination,office scheduler
branch_id,approved routing map,branch-east,maps to permitted calendar,branch reference,branch administrator
calendar_id,destination configuration,cal-east,exact authorized branch mapping,target resource,integration lead
time_zone,branch configuration,America/New_York,local time and offset agree,event time zone,office scheduler
start,caller-approved request,2026-11-02T09:00:00-05:00,round-trip local time is identical,event start,office scheduler
end,approved duration rule,2026-11-02T10:00:00-05:00,after start and approved duration,event end,office scheduler
record_id,destination or supported ID allocator,event-001,stable reconciliation reference,one intended record,integration lead
expected_version,last authoritative read,v1,matches current version before edit,conditional change,integration lead
permissions,authorized access configuration,event read and write,operation allowed on target calendar,no permission escalation,account administrator
operation,caller-approved operation,create,create or change or cancel,only intended mutation,office scheduler

```

| Test requirement | Google Calendar example | Contract question |
|---|---|---|
| Inspect availability | `calendar.events.freebusy` covers availability on accessible calendars | Which exact calendars may this identity inspect? |
| Read event details | `calendar.events.readonly` | Can the integration locate and verify the intended record? |
| Create, change and delete events | `calendar.events.owned` applies to owned calendars; other configurations require their appropriate scope | Does the authorized identity have the required operation on this destination? |
| Change sharing or calendar configuration | Separate ACL/calendar scopes exist | Why would a booking connection need this administrative power? |

Google recommends the narrowest scopes that meet the application’s requirements. Its permission model is an example, not a portable permission specification for every scheduling product. Do not request account-wide administration merely to resolve a failed booking test. [Google Calendar authorization scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/auth)

## 4. Test three different concurrency problems

**One request delivered twice.** Keep the same operation identity and reconcile an existing result. If the destination supports client-assigned identifiers, follow its collision rules. A duplicate-identifier response requires inspection of the existing record, not an automatic new identifier that creates another appointment.

**Two customers choosing the same opening.** Their request IDs are different. Both might observe free time before either writes. Your authoritative scheduling system needs its own supported capacity-control mechanism. A stable request ID alone offers no protection against this race; a bare read/write calendar pair does not guarantee exclusive booking.

**An employee editing an existing appointment.** Read its version, submit a conditional modification and resolve changes rather than overwriting them blindly. Google Calendar supports `If-Match` with the previously read `etag` for update/delete operations. A changed resource produces HTTP 412. Conditional insertion is different: the documented insert safeguard concerns an existing resource ID, not two events occupying the same time. [Google Calendar resource versioning](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/version-resources)

## 5. Give each failure a bounded recovery path

| Failure | Proposed application behavior |
|---|---|
| Invalid payload | Correct the input; do not loop on the same invalid request. |
| Missing authorization or access | Stop that operation and route to the authorized administrator; never broaden credentials automatically. |
| Duplicate identifier | Inspect the existing record and compare the intended operation before deciding whether it is the same result. |
| Stale record version | Read the current record and resolve the competing change; do not blindly overwrite it. |
| Rate limiting | Use the platform’s documented backoff guidance with an explicit attempt/time budget and exception owner. |
| Write timeout | Treat persistence as unknown; reconcile before any retry that could create another record. |
| Cancellation failure | Keep cancellation pending until the authoritative destination supplies sufficient evidence of the intended state. |

Google documents invalid-request errors, duplicate IDs, stale-version failures, and rate-limit responses including 403/429. Error reasons matter alongside HTTP status; a 403 is not always the same problem. Its guidance includes exponential backoff for retryable failures. Set a bounded application policy rather than promising indefinite recovery. The uncertainty handling above is a proposed design, not a claim that a timeout proves success or failure. [Google Calendar error handling](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/errors)

## 6. Run the synthetic failure fixtures

Use invented customers and a provider-supported test environment. The companion local fixture runner models the acceptance rules without network access or credentials. It tests a deliberately small reference model, not a live connector, API compliance, or production concurrency. The model uses one synthetic east branch and rejects stale updates; successful appointment changes are intentionally unsupported rather than simulated as verified writes. An integration team must replay equivalent failures against its authorized adapter before signing off.

| Fixture and injected condition | Expected authoritative result | Caller wording | Owner and required evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duplicate request: deliver `req-001` twice | One intended record; both deliveries resolve to its ID | “Your appointment is confirmed” only after verification | Integration lead: request-to-record mapping and record count |
| Wrong branch: route east request to west calendar | No new record | “The office needs to verify the location before confirming” | Branch administrator: approved map and rejected target |
| Partial availability: one required calendar returns an error | No new record | “I cannot verify that opening yet” | Integration lead: per-calendar response and exception ID |
| Calendar unavailable: destination lookup cannot complete | No new record or assumed availability | “The office must verify availability” | Integration lead: lookup failure and retry/exception decision |
| Local-time mismatch: New York November time supplied with the wrong offset | No new record | “Let’s verify the local time before confirming” | Scheduler: local time, zone, offset and conversion |
| Stale update: employee edits version 1 into version 2 before agent writes | Employee’s version preserved; change remains unresolved | “Your requested change is pending review” | Scheduler: both versions and rejected conditional update |
| Write timeout after persistence | Original record recovered; no second record | Confirmation only after inspection of that record | Integration lead: original operation ID, timeout and read-back |
| Write timeout before persistence, reconciliation unavailable | No confirmation and no speculative replacement write | “Your request is awaiting verification” | Integration lead: uncertainty state and assigned exception |
| Cancellation during pending creation, then failed cancellation | Persisted record remains active; cancellation stays pending; booking confirmation suppressed | “Your cancellation request is pending verification” | Scheduler: cancellation intent, resulting record and failure |

For a successful cancellation, replace the injected failure with a verified terminal result and assert that no active booking remains. A not-found response by itself may reflect access or lookup problems; use the destination’s documented behavior and your identity checks before treating it as cancellation evidence.

Run the supplied offline file with `python centralized-scheduling-fixtures.py` using a Python installation with IANA time-zone data. Passing assertions establish only that this small reference model meets its fixtures; they do not certify your selected connector.

## 7. Accept the connection only with evidence

Require an operation log that connects the input, authorized destination, attempted mutation, inspected result, customer message and exception owner. Mask personal data in review copies. Reject a test that passes only because the system sends reassuring language while the destination is unknown.

Stop testing and disable the affected mutation path if it writes to an unintended branch, loses a competing edit or duplicates a request. Preserve evidence and reconcile affected records through an authorized operator; do not run a bulk-delete “rollback” against live calendars.

**Next step:** establish what your office means by a requested versus confirmed appointment in the [appointment-booking guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/appointment-booking), then give this record contract to the team implementing your chosen connection. For platform-specific evaluation, use the [Jobber answering-service guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/jobber-answering-service) or [ServiceTitan answering-service guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/servicetitan-answering-service). These links are buying-context resources, not proof that any particular integration passes these tests.

sections.title: Define which job you are buying
paragraphs:
Use four separate requirements in your provider brief:

| Requirement | Question to resolve |

| Explain the fee | Can the service state your approved amount and terms without inventing a quote? |
| Deliver a payment route | Can it share an authorized hosted link through a supported channel? |
| Process the payment | Who enters or receives sensitive payment information, in which system? |
| Confirm the next step | Who verifies payment status and authorizes the appointment or office follow-up? |

Payment collection is a real answering-service category, but implementations differ. Smith.ai’s current feature page distinguishes AI-led payment conversations from human agents handling transactions. Treat that as a description of that provider’s offering, not a capability shared by every AI receptionist. [Smith.ai payment collection](https://smith.ai/features/payment-collection-service)

For a service-call deposit, specify whether the approved amount applies to a diagnostic visit, an assessment or another defined service. The receptionist should not calculate an unapproved repair price from the caller’s description.

sections.title: Compare hosted checkout with a spoken-card workflow
paragraphs:
With hosted checkout, the customer enters payment details on the payment provider’s page rather than reading them into an ordinary intake conversation. Stripe documents shareable Payment Links leading to a Stripe-hosted page. It also distinguishes reusable Payment Links from invoices directed to a specific customer. [Stripe Payment Links](https://docs.stripe.com/payment-links)

That distinction matters operationally. Ask your payment owner whether the approved route identifies the correct customer and service request. A generic link reaching a successful checkout does not, by itself, explain which job the payment belongs to.

A spoken-card workflow requires a different review. Identify the authorized person or system receiving the information, every recording or transcript in the route, and the controls documented for that exact arrangement. Do not infer suitability merely because an agent can type into a payment screen.

Neither option automatically establishes compliance. Have your payment provider and responsible security owner assess the actual setup before use.

sections.title: Keep sensitive details out of ordinary call records
paragraphs:
PCI SSC’s current FAQ states that retaining card validation codes in digital audio after authorization violates PCI DSS Requirement 3.3.1, including when that information is encrypted. It advises preventing capture where possible and enabling supported suppression or redaction. [PCI SSC voice-recording FAQ](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/faqs/1210/)

For an ordinary intake workflow, give the receptionist a clear boundary: do not request card details for a call summary, email, text message or CRM note. If a caller starts reading them aloud, redirect to the approved payment route. If sensitive information has already entered a recording or record, notify the designated security owner and follow the reviewed incident procedure; do not improvise a deletion promise.

The appropriate office note describes the action and status—not the card credentials. For example: “Approved payment route provided; payment confirmation pending review.” This is an illustrative status, not a real customer record.

sections.title: Do not confuse a sent link with a paid deposit
paragraphs:
Agree on distinct statuses before enabling the workflow:

- **Payment requested:** the approved request was explained.
- **Route provided:** the link or authorized handoff was delivered.
- **Confirmation pending:** payment has not yet been verified by the responsible system or person.
- **Payment confirmed:** the authorized reviewer has checked the relevant payment record.
- **Appointment confirmed:** an authorized booking process has accepted the appointment.

These are proposed operating labels, not Stripe or Revo status names. Your payment owner should define which processor event permits each transition. A caller saying “I clicked it,” or an agent sending a link, is not sufficient payment evidence.

Keep payment and scheduling decisions separate. If the calendar or payment connection is unavailable, explain that confirmation remains pending. Do not promise a visit merely because the customer attempted payment.

sections.title: Give exceptions a named owner
paragraphs:
Ask who handles an abandoned checkout, an apparent duplicate payment, a disputed amount and a requested refund. Reception instructions should not independently authorize discounts, refunds or additional charges.

For a customer who cannot use the link, provide the business’s approved alternative or an office callback. Do not convert the call into an unreviewed card-collection process just to complete it quickly.

Require a non-sensitive reconciliation record: the relevant job or request reference, payment reference where approved, responsible reviewer and resulting next action. Limit access according to the business’s reviewed policy.

sections.title: Evaluate the workflow without real customer money
paragraphs:
Before contracting, request an authorized sandbox demonstration using fictional customers and provider-approved test data. These are proposed checks; none were performed for this article.

1. The approved amount and service description are stated accurately.
2. The payment route identifies the intended request.
3. Incomplete checkout remains pending rather than being reported as paid.
4. A repeated caller does not trigger an automatic second request or charge.
5. A failed connection produces a clear office handoff.
6. Call notes contain no payment credentials.
7. A refund request reaches someone with the required authority.

Separate answering fees, payment-provider charges, implementation work and staff reconciliation when requesting a quote. This article supplies no price, fee estimate or savings guarantee.

sections.title: Where Revo fits—and what still needs verification
paragraphs:
If payment handling is essential to your purchase, ask Revo directly which parts of the conversation and handoff it currently supports. A general booking or intake feature does not prove payment processing, hosted-link delivery or a named integration.

**Does a hosted link establish compliance?** No. The business still needs review of its actual systems, responsibilities and configuration.

**Does this page claim that Revo processes payments?** No. That capability and any named payment connection remain unverified.

That distinction matters operationally. Ask your payment owner whether the approved route identifies the correct customer and service request. A generic link reaching a successful checkout does not, by itself, explain which job the payment belongs to.

A spoken-card workflow requires a different review. Identify the authorized person or system receiving the information, every recording or transcript in the route, and the controls documented for that exact arrangement. Do not infer suitability merely because an agent can type into a payment screen.

Neither option automatically establishes compliance. Have your payment provider and responsible security owner assess the actual setup before use.

The appropriate office note describes the action and status—not the card credentials. For example: “Approved payment route provided; payment confirmation pending review.” This is an illustrative status, not a real customer record.

- **Payment requested:** the approved request was explained.
- **Route provided:** the link or authorized handoff was delivered.
- **Confirmation pending:** payment has not yet been verified by the responsible system or person.
- **Payment confirmed:** the authorized reviewer has checked the relevant payment record.
- **Appointment confirmed:** an authorized booking process has accepted the appointment.

2. The payment route identifies the intended request.
3. Incomplete checkout remains pending rather than being reported as paid.
4. A repeated caller does not trigger an automatic second request or charge.
5. A failed connection produces a clear office handoff.
6. Call notes contain no payment credentials.
7. A refund request reaches someone with the required authority.

Separate answering fees, payment-provider charges, implementation work and staff reconciliation when requesting a quote. This article supplies no price, fee estimate or savings guarantee.

sections.title: Separate four kinds of work
paragraphs:
One product may combine several of these functions. Evaluate each separately rather than assuming that access to one gives permission for the others. These are task types, not permission levels: even a capture tool can speak to a customer or store personal information. Review its actual access and actions separately.

| Workflow | Input → output | Home-service example | Important boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capture and conversation | A caller's statements and approved instructions → a structured request or response | Collect a plumbing inquiry for office review | Capture what the caller said; do not turn a symptom into a diagnosis or an unconfirmed visit into a booking. |
| Draft generation | Approved facts and an editing request → proposed text | Rewrite an existing cleaning-service description | A draft is not approved for publication, pricing changes or campaign delivery. |
| Read-only analysis | An authorized, defined dataset → an answer with supporting records | Summarize recorded request types for a specified week | Check the date range, units and underlying records; a plausible explanation is not proof. |
| Permitted system action | A validated request and explicit authority → a changed record | Create an appointment in a supported scheduling system | A proposed time is not a successful write. Permissions, confirmation and recovery need separate verification. |

These categories are not hypothetical product labels. Housecall Pro describes CSR AI for customer communication, Marketing AI for drafting and Analyst AI for business-data questions. Its page distinguishes included functions from separately paid call answering. That is evidence of different task categories, not a recommendation to buy its suite or a claim that every tool offers them. [Housecall Pro AI Team](https://www.housecallpro.com/features/ai-team/).

sections.title: Find a problem before choosing an AI feature
paragraphs:
Write the problem as an observable task: “The office calls people back because requests lack a return number,” rather than “We need AI.” Keep a small, authorized sample of the work that demonstrates the issue. If you cannot show the recurring problem, investigate before buying a tool.

Next, consider a non-AI fix. An intake form, a maintained service-description template or a saved report may solve the same problem. Compare AI against that practical alternative, not against doing nothing.

Use these questions to narrow the choice:

1. **Is the source usable?** Identify the current service list, approved wording or dataset. Conflicting instructions are a cleanup task first, not permission for the tool to choose whichever version it finds.
2. **Can someone check the result?** Name the person who understands the work and can inspect an output against its source. If nobody can judge correctness, defer the workflow.
3. **Does the output stay inside the office?** A draft can wait for review. A spoken promise, sent message or changed customer record may already affect someone before a reviewer sees it.
4. **Can the work return to a manual process?** Describe how to stop the workflow and resolve anything left pending. Deleting an AI draft is different from undoing an appointment change.

Data preparation matters even in purpose-built software. Housecall Pro's CSR AI documentation ties booking behavior to enabled services, service descriptions, booking settings and available windows; it also acknowledges that correct setup does not eliminate every mistake. [CSR AI setup guidance](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/12001958-csr-ai-best-practices-and-faqs).

sections.title: Use a workflow-choice card, not an invented ROI score
paragraphs:
Fill one card for each plausible task, then choose **one** for a bounded test. Use the [blank worksheet and fictional examples](workflow-choice-worksheet.md).

| Record on the card | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| Task and observed bottleneck | The specific work being considered, with evidence rather than a general desire to automate |
| Non-AI alternative | The existing template, form, report or manual process to compare against |
| Input source and version | Which facts or records are authoritative, and what is missing |
| Expected output and workflow type | Whether you need capture, a draft, analysis or an external action |
| Permitted action and human owner | What may happen without another approval, and who handles exceptions |
| Consequence of error | Who could be affected and whether the effect is reversible |
| Acceptance conditions and evidence | What the reviewer must observe before deciding the test is useful |
| Fallback and decision | How to stop safely; whether to test, revise or defer the task |

Do not total these fields into a universal “automation score.” A low-frequency action can still have a serious consequence. Select a workflow whose problem, inputs, reviewer and boundaries are all clear; defer one with unresolved authority or unreliable source data.

NIST's AI Risk Management Framework is voluntary guidance for considering risk in AI design, use and evaluation. The worksheet here is an editorial aid, not a NIST certification or a claim that a tool is risk-free. [NIST AI RMF](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework).

sections.title: Two offices can reasonably choose different first workflows
paragraphs:
### Office A: incomplete service requests

In this fictional example, a plumbing office repeatedly has to recover missing callback details. Its useful first experiment is **capture**, not autonomous scheduling. The expected output is a request containing the caller's stated need, a return number when supplied and clearly marked missing information.

The office manager owns review. The test cannot diagnose the problem, quote a repair price or promise a visit. A missing return number must stay missing, not be invented. This office defers its other candidate—automatic booking—because appointment-write authority and recovery are unresolved. The simpler alternative is a revised intake form or script. If that solves the capture problem, the office may not need an AI tool for it.

### Office B: repeated rewriting of approved descriptions

In this fictional example, a cleaning-business owner already has accurate descriptions but repeatedly rewrites them for different page lengths. The first experiment is **draft generation**. It does not require customer records, phone access or scheduling permissions.

The owner checks whether each draft preserves the approved services and exclusions. An added guarantee, price or service is a failure to correct, not creative improvement. The output stays unpublished until approved. This office defers its other candidate—AI analysis of request patterns—because its records do not yet distinguish new inquiries from repeat contacts. The simpler alternative for drafting is a reusable short-and-long description template.

Neither example establishes which task is best for every business. It shows why the initial decision should follow the work rather than a vendor's list of features.

sections.title: Test the choice without quietly expanding its authority
paragraphs:
Begin with fictional inputs or data you are authorized to use. Keep customer outreach, live record changes, payments and field-safety decisions outside this initial test. For conversation tools, use authorized test conversations rather than routing unsuspecting callers into an experiment.

Create four cases for the chosen task:

| Case | Capture example | Drafting example |
|---|---|---|
| Normal input | A stated service request with a callback number | A description containing the approved service and exclusions |
| Missing information | No callback number supplied | No approved price supplied |
| Outdated or conflicting source | Old service-area instructions conflict with the current version | An old description contains a guarantee absent from the current approved text |
| Outside the allowed scope | The caller asks for a diagnosis or a confirmed visit | The request asks the tool to publish the draft or invent a discount |

Write the expected behavior before running each case. Preserve the input version, actual output, correction needed and reviewer decision. An unresolved source conflict should pause the affected answer or action for review, not silently become a guessed fact.

Keep the test proportionate. This is a task-selection exercise, not proof that a system is ready for unattended customer use. Once capture is the chosen workflow, the separate [receptionist selection guide](/ai-answering-service/choose-virtual-receptionist) covers provider requirements, and the [answering-service trial guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-free-trial) covers evaluating an offer.

sections.title: Decide whether to retain, revise or stop
paragraphs:
Compare the test with the manual or template-based alternative. Record output quality, correction effort, unresolved exceptions and the staff time actually observed. Include review and cleanup time; do not count only the seconds spent generating an answer. A small fictional test does not establish future revenue, time savings or accuracy rates.

- **Retain for further evaluation** when the bounded task meets the written acceptance conditions and the reviewer can verify its outputs. This is not authorization to add new actions.
- **Revise and retest** when a specific source, instruction or workflow problem can be corrected. Keep the same scope so the comparison remains meaningful.
- **Stop or defer** when authority is unclear, outputs cannot be checked or correction work defeats the purpose. Return to the stated manual process and review any pending work.

If call handling is the selected task, keep inquiries, bookings and completed jobs separate when measuring later results. A captured request is not a sold job. Use the existing [conversion measurement guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-conversion-rate-comparison) rather than treating every AI interaction as revenue.

sections.title: Where Revo fits
paragraphs:
Revo's published services include answering, lead intake and call summaries. If those match the task you selected, use the [current service description](https://www.revoapp.ai/services.html) to begin a configuration discussion. Confirm supported actions and plan scope before allowing booking or transfers. This guide does not present Revo as a general marketing-writing tool, business-analysis platform or autonomous field decision-maker.

The next step is small: complete one workflow-choice card and name its reviewer. If the card exposes a missing source or unclear authority, resolving that is progress—even when the right decision is not to automate yet.

1. **Is the source usable?** Identify the current service list, approved wording or dataset. Conflicting instructions are a cleanup task first, not permission for the tool to choose whichever version it finds.
2. **Can someone check the result?** Name the person who understands the work and can inspect an output against its source. If nobody can judge correctness, defer the workflow.
3. **Does the output stay inside the office?** A draft can wait for review. A spoken promise, sent message or changed customer record may already affect someone before a reviewer sees it.
4. **Can the work return to a manual process?** Describe how to stop the workflow and resolve anything left pending. Deleting an AI draft is different from undoing an appointment change.

## Use a workflow-choice card, not an invented ROI score

Fill one card for each plausible task, then choose **one** for a bounded test. Use the [blank worksheet and fictional examples](workflow-choice-worksheet.md).

| Record on the card | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| Task and observed bottleneck | The specific work being considered, with evidence rather than a general desire to automate |
| Non-AI alternative | The existing template, form, report or manual process to compare against |
| Input source and version | Which facts or records are authoritative, and what is missing |
| Expected output and workflow type | Whether you need capture, a draft, analysis or an external action |
| Permitted action and human owner | What may happen without another approval, and who handles exceptions |
| Consequence of error | Who could be affected and whether the effect is reversible |
| Acceptance conditions and evidence | What the reviewer must observe before deciding the test is useful |
| Fallback and decision | How to stop safely; whether to test, revise or defer the task |

Do not total these fields into a universal “automation score.” A low-frequency action can still have a serious consequence. Select a workflow whose problem, inputs, reviewer and boundaries are all clear; defer one with unresolved authority or unreliable source data.

### Office A: incomplete service requests

This office defers its other candidate—automatic booking—because appointment-write authority and recovery are unresolved. The simpler alternative is a revised intake form or script. ### Office B: repeated rewriting of approved descriptions

In this fictional example, a cleaning-business owner already has accurate descriptions but repeatedly rewrites them for different page lengths. The first experiment is **draft generation**. It does not require customer records, phone access or scheduling permissions.

The owner checks whether each draft preserves the approved services and exclusions. An added guarantee, price or service is a failure to correct, not creative improvement. The output stays unpublished until approved. This office defers its other candidate—AI analysis of request patterns—because its records do not yet distinguish new inquiries from repeat contacts. The simpler alternative for drafting is a reusable short-and-long description template.

Neither example establishes which task is best for every business. It shows why the initial decision should follow the work rather than a vendor's list of features.

## Test the choice without quietly expanding its authority

Begin with fictional inputs or data you are authorized to use. Keep customer outreach, live record changes, payments and field-safety decisions outside this initial test. For conversation tools, use authorized test conversations rather than routing unsuspecting callers into an experiment.

Create four cases for the chosen task:

| Case | Capture example | Drafting example |
|---|---|---|
| Normal input | A stated service request with a callback number | A description containing the approved service and exclusions |
| Missing information | No callback number supplied | No approved price supplied |
| Outdated or conflicting source | Old service-area instructions conflict with the current version | An old description contains a guarantee absent from the current approved text |
| Outside the allowed scope | The caller asks for a diagnosis or a confirmed visit | The request asks the tool to publish the draft or invent a discount |

Write the expected behavior before running each case. Preserve the input version, actual output, correction needed and reviewer decision. An unresolved source conflict should pause the affected answer or action for review, not silently become a guessed fact.

Keep the test proportionate. This is a task-selection exercise, not proof that a system is ready for unattended customer use. ## Decide whether to retain, revise or stop

Compare the test with the manual or template-based alternative. Record output quality, correction effort, unresolved exceptions and the staff time actually observed. Include review and cleanup time; do not count only the seconds spent generating an answer. A small fictional test does not establish future revenue, time savings or accuracy rates.

- **Retain for further evaluation** when the bounded task meets the written acceptance conditions and the reviewer can verify its outputs. This is not authorization to add new actions.
- **Revise and retest** when a specific source, instruction or workflow problem can be corrected. Keep the same scope so the comparison remains meaningful.
- **Stop or defer** when authority is unclear, outputs cannot be checked or correction work defeats the purpose. Return to the stated manual process and review any pending work.

If call handling is the selected task, keep inquiries, bookings and completed jobs separate when measuring later results. A captured request is not a sold job. Use the existing [conversion measurement guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-conversion-rate-comparison) rather than treating every AI interaction as revenue.

## Where Revo fits

Revo's published services include answering, lead intake and call summaries. If those match the task you selected, use the [current service description](https://www.revoapp.ai/services.html) to begin a configuration discussion. Confirm supported actions and plan scope before allowing booking or transfers. This guide does not present Revo as a general marketing-writing tool, business-analysis platform or autonomous field decision-maker.

The next step is small: complete one workflow-choice card and name its reviewer. If the card exposes a missing source or unclear authority, resolving that is progress—even when the right decision is not to automate yet.
